title: V6 processors receive a flat OperationWithContext list via onOperations instead of grouped strands via onStrands
content:
The v6 Reactor replaced `onStrands(strands: InternalTransmitterUpdate[])` with `onOperations(operations: OperationWithContext[])`. Each OperationWithContext destructures as `{ operation, context }` where context has `documentId`, `documentType`, `scope`, `branch`, `ordinal` (global monotonic counter for cross-document ordering), and optional `resultingState` (JSON string). Operation access changed: `operation.type` -> `operation.action.type`, `operation.input` -> `operation.action.input`, `operation.timestamp` -> `operation.action.timestampUtcMs`. Steady-state live routing delivers each matching operation once, in global-ordinal order, but delivery is not exactly-once overall: backfill and replay are an explicit part of the processor contract, so idempotence guards (`clearSource` / `index === 0` rebuilds) are still recommended. The manager pages through history via `operationIndex.getSinceOrdinal(lastOrdinal)` when a factory registers against a drive that already has history, after a restart to replay the gap missed while the reactor was down, and when `tracked.retry()` re-activates an errored processor and re-runs backfill. Cursors persist in the `ProcessorCursor` table keyed by `processorId`, and on startup the manager rehydrates them and catch-up replays the gap. Factory signature changed from `(driveId: string)` to `(driveHeader: PHDocumentHeader, processorApp?: ProcessorApp)` with outer parameter changing from direct dependencies to `IProcessorHostModule`.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: The IProcessor interface simplified from strand-based to flat operation-based with per-operation context including global ordinal.
